title: Domestic Investors Accumulate BBCA, BBRI, and TLKM Shares Amid MSCI Downgrade Turmoil
body: Between October 16 and 23, 2026, domestic investors accumulated blue-chip stocks amid market turmoil following MSCI's announcement of consultations to downgrade Indonesia from emerging markets to standalone markets. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) recorded the largest overall net buy of Rp 4.36 trillion despite foreign net sell of Rp 5.22 trillion, while PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) and PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) posted overall net buys of Rp 1.33 trillion and Rp 1.31 trillion against foreign net sells of Rp 3.26 trillion and Rp 663 billion respectively. The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) plunged 11.57% to 5,185 on October 16 before recovering to close at 5,439 on October 23. Separately, BBCA planned a share buyback on October 19-21, 2026, part of a program approved at its March 2026 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders, with management not yet detailing the fund allocation.

title: KB Valbury Sekuritas Recommends Trading Buy on PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) Shares
body: KB Valbury Sekuritas placed PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) on its watchlist for Monday trading (26/10/2026) and recommended a trading buy with a daily price target of Rp 2,940, an entry range of Rp 2,850–2,910, resistance at Rp 2,940, support at Rp 2,850, and a stop loss at Rp 2,760. BBRI closed up 0.3% at Rp 2,910 on Friday (23/10/2026), gaining 10.2% over the past week but falling 8.49% over the past month and 20.49% year to date. BRI management also announced the second phase of a share buyback program scheduled for 22 October 2026 to 21 January 2027, worth a maximum of Rp 1 trillion funded from internal cash, with resulting treasury stock not to exceed 10% of paid-up capital.

title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) Plans Second-Phase Share Buyback of Up to Rp1 Trillion
body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) announced a second-phase share buyback of up to Rp1 trillion, scheduled to run from 22 October 2026 to 21 January 2027, amid significantly fluctuating capital market conditions. The buyback follows OJK Regulation Number 13 of 2023 and an OJK letter dated 9 September 2026 on buyback policies for public companies in significantly fluctuating markets. Corporate Secretary Dhanny said the move aims to enhance shareholder value and reflects management's confidence in BRI's business fundamentals and long-term growth prospects. On a pro forma consolidated basis as of 30 June 2026 after accounting for the buyback, BRI's Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) stands at a strong 21.42% and Return on Equity (ROE) at 18.80%. The repurchased shares are planned for employee and/or Directors and Board of Commissioners ownership programs, with transfer subject to approval at a General Meeting of Shareholders.

title: Indonesian Issuers Including BBRI, BBCA, TLKM, JSMR, and AMMN Prepare or Extend Share Buyback Programs
body: Several issuers on the Indonesia Stock Exchange are preparing, continuing, or studying share buyback programs amid a recent correction in the composite stock price index. PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) is preparing a second-stage buyback of up to Rp1 trillion, scheduled for 22 October 2026 to 21 January 2027 with OJK approval, after realizing about Rp90.37 billion of a Rp500 billion allocation in its previous program. PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM) plans to accelerate its regular buyback of up to Rp4 trillion, with more than Rp3 trillion remaining as of 19 October 2026, separately from a completed repurchase of 15,956,199 shares worth Rp36.54 billion at Rp2,290 per share tied to dissenting shareholders of its wholesale fiber connectivity spin-off. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) extended its buyback period from 19-21 October to 19-23 October 2026, with around Rp3.5 trillion realized of a Rp5 trillion program valid until March 2027. PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) is studying a potential buyback without announced value or schedule, while PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) is allocating about Rp1 trillion from internal cash for a buyback running 22 October 2026 to 22 January 2027.

title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) Announces Phase II Share Buyback of Up to Rp1 Trillion
body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) announced a Phase II share buyback of up to Rp1 trillion, to run from 22 October 2026 to 21 January 2027, citing significantly fluctuating capital market conditions. The buyback follows OJK Regulation Number 13 of 2023 and OJK letter S-112/D.04/2026 on buybacks during significantly fluctuating markets. Management said the move reflects confidence in the company's fundamentals and long-term growth, with repurchased shares planned for employee and/or Director and Commissioner stock ownership programs pending GMS approval. On a pro forma basis as of 30 June 2026, the company's consolidated Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) stands at 21.42% and Return on Equity (ROE) at 18.80%, indicating adequate capital capacity.

title: Popular News Roundup: Russia Draws Down Gold Reserves, GEMS Pays Interim Dividend, BBCA and BBRI Buybacks, ADMR Dividend Outlook
body: This roundup of five popular investor.id stories covers Bank of Russia's sale of 200,000 troy ounces (6.2 tons) of gold in September 2026, cutting reserves to 72.8 million troy ounces (2,264 tons), the lowest since late 2019, after liquidating about 62 tons since December 2025 to fund the federal deficit. PT Golden Energy Mines Tbk (GEMS), a coal mining issuer of the Sinar Mas Group, pays an interim dividend of US$200 million, or Rp611.93 per share (US$0,034), on 22 October 2026 using a BI middle rate of Rp17,996 per US dollar. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) recorded the largest foreign net buy of Rp448.09 billion on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, closing up 1.4% at Rp5,275, and extended its share buyback to 23 October 2026. PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) announced a phase II 2026 buyback of up to Rp1 trillion from internal cash, with treasury stock not exceeding 10% of placed capital. PT Alamtri Minerals Indonesia Tbk (ADMR), an affiliate of Boy Thohir, is seen as an accumulation opportunity after its net cash flow turned positive at US$210 million in 2026, with projected 2027 cash flow of US$533 million supporting an estimated Rp127 per share dividend for 2027.

title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) Plans Share Buyback of Up to Rp1 Trillion, Citing Confidence in Long-Term Prospects
body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) announced a Stage II share buyback plan of up to Rp1 trillion, disclosed via information disclosure on Thursday (22/10), to run from 22 October 2026 to 21 January 2027 under POJK Number 13 of 2023 and OJK Letter Number S-112/D.04/2026. Corporate Secretary Dhanny said the plan reflects management's confidence in the strength of the company's business fundamentals and long-term growth prospects, amid significantly fluctuating capital market conditions. Based on pro forma calculations against the consolidated financial condition as of 30 June 2026, the Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) remains strong at 21.42 percent and Return on Equity (ROE) stands at 18.80 percent. Repurchased shares are planned for employee stock ownership and/or the Direksi and Dewan Komisaris programs, with the transfer to take effect only after approval at a General Meeting of Shareholders (RUPS).

title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) Plans Phase II Share Buyback of Up to Rp 1 Trillion
body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) announced on Thursday, October 22, a Phase II share buyback plan of up to Rp 1 trillion, to run from October 22, 2026 to January 21, 2027, under POJK Number 13 of 2023 and OJK letter S-112/D.04/2026 on buybacks during significantly fluctuating markets. The company said the buyback reflects management's confidence in its business fundamentals and long-term growth prospects, with repurchased shares planned for employee and/or director and commissioner ownership programs after GMS approval. On a pro forma basis as of June 30, 2026, BBRI's consolidated Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) would remain strong at 21.42% and Return on Equity (ROE) at 18.80%. The buyback will be executed at prices the company deems fair, while maintaining healthy capital structure and good corporate governance.

title: BRI Prepares Rp1 Trillion Share Buyback Through January 2027
body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) plans a second-stage share buyback of up to Rp1 trillion, running from 22 October 2026 to 21 January 2027, in line with OJK Regulation Number 13 of 2023 on buybacks during significantly fluctuating market conditions. The bank said the buyback reflects confidence in its business fundamentals and long-term growth, with repurchased shares planned for employee stock ownership and/or Director and Board of Commissioners programs after GMS approval. On a pro forma basis after the buyback, BRI's consolidated capital adequacy ratio as of 30 June 2026 is estimated to remain at 21.42%, with a return on equity of 18.80%.

title: 19 State-Owned Enterprise Stocks Close Higher Amid Massive Buying and Buyback Programs
body: Nineteen state-owned enterprise (SOE) stocks closed higher across banking, telecommunications, construction, and energy sectors, supported by large-scale buying and share buyback programs. The biggest gainers included PT PP Properti Tbk (PPRO) up 7.14% to Rp15, PT Jasa Marga (Persero) Tbk (JSMR) up 5.11% to Rp2,470, PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) up 4.92% to Rp3,410, and PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) up 4.05% to Rp3,850, while PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) rose 4.41% to Rp2,840. BBRI, BMRI, PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM), BBNI, and ANTM helped lift the IHSG, which closed up 1.12% at 5,387.91 on volume of 331.29 million lots worth Rp15.31 trillion. BMRI allocated Rp1.17 trillion for a buyback running April 30, 2026 to April 29, 2027, BBNI allocated Rp627 billion for July 27 to October 26, 2026, and Telkom moved to accelerate its Rp4 trillion buyback approved at the June 8, 2026 AGM, with over Rp3 trillion remaining as of October 19, 2026. BPI Danantara Indonesia, through Chief Investment Officer Pandu Sjahrir, said it has begun buying Indonesian stocks, viewing current market pressure on the IHSG as an investment opportunity and planning to increase holdings in SOE stocks citing strong fundamentals and attractive valuations.

title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) Plans Rp1 Trillion Share Buyback Following OJK Approval
body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) has secured OJK approval, via letter number S-210/PB.21/2026 dated 22 October 2026, to conduct a share buyback of up to Rp1 trillion. The buyback will run from 22 October 2026 to 21 January 2027 on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX), executed gradually or all at once using internal cash, as part of the second phase of buyback amid significant market fluctuation in 2026 under POJK Number 13 of 2023. BBRI expects transaction costs of up to 0.20% of the buyback value, with repurchased shares not exceeding 10% of placed capital. Based on a simulation using consolidated financials as of 30 June 2026, total assets are projected to fall from Rp2,342.8 trillion to Rp2,341.8 trillion, total equity from Rp333.62 trillion to Rp332.62 trillion, net profit remaining at Rp31.18 trillion, EPS rising from Rp206.94 to Rp207.50, CAR slipping from 21.49% to 21.42%, and ROE increasing from 18.79% to 18.80%. The repurchased shares are planned for employee and/or director and commissioner stock ownership programs, subject to approval at a General Meeting of Shareholders (GMS).

title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) Announces Second-Phase Share Buyback of Up to Rp 1 Trillion
body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) plans to conduct a second-phase share buyback in 2026 amid significantly fluctuating market conditions. The buyback value is estimated at a maximum of Rp 1 trillion, funded from the company's internal cash, with intermediary broker commissions and other costs estimated at no more than 0.20% of the buyback value. The buyback period is estimated to run from October 22, 2026 to January 21, 2027. The resulting treasury stock will not exceed 10% of the company's issued capital, in accordance with applicable regulations.

title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) launches Rp1 trillion buyback after stock hits Auto Reject Bottom
body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), the Indonesian state-owned bank with the largest market capitalization, announced a Rp1 trillion share buyback running from 22 October 2026 to 21 January 2027, its second buyback of 2026 after a Rp500 billion program from 12 June to 11 September 2026 for its Management and Employee Stock Option Plan (MESOP). The second-stage buyback, funded with internal cash under POJK 13/2023 and POJK 29/2023, is expected to absorb up to 0.20% of outstanding shares, with all repurchased shares also allocated to MESOP subject to shareholder approval for transfer. The buyback follows a 14.48% drop in BBRI's share price on 16 October amid market reaction to MSCI's proposal to downgrade Indonesia from Emerging to Standalone Market, which sent the IHSG into a 30-minute trading halt after falling more than 7%, leaving BBRI's price held at the Auto Reject Bottom (ARB) for a day. The stock has since rebounded more than 14% from its early-week low as of 21 October, though it remains down more than 21% year to date.

title: IHSG Turns Green Supported by State-Owned Enterprise Stocks Amid Buyback Programs and Danantara Entry Plans
body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) rose 53.07 points or 1% to 5,381.43 at 09:56 WIB during mid-morning trading, after falling as much as 2% at the open, supported mainly by state-owned enterprise (BUMN) stocks including PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM), PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI), and PT Aneka Tambang (Persero) Tbk (ANTM). The rebound coincided with multiple issuers on the Indonesia Stock Exchange conducting share buybacks from October to December 2026: Bank Mandiri allocated Rp1.17 trillion for the period April 30, 2026 to April 29, 2027, Bank Negara Indonesia allocated Rp627 billion for July 27, 2026 to October 26, 2026, and Telkom is accelerating its buyback of up to Rp4 trillion approved at the June 8, 2026 annual shareholders meeting, with more than Rp3 trillion remaining as of October 19, 2026. Danantara CEO Rosan Roeslani called the share price decline a long-term investment opportunity, while COO Dony Oskaria, who also heads BP BUMN, opened the possibility of increasing BUMN share ownership, though Danantara has not specified which stocks or amounts. Investors are also watching whether the gains hold following heavy selling two days earlier and awaiting MSCI's decision on Indonesia's market status.

title: Trillions of Rupiah Ready to Enter the Market as 10 Issuers Prepare Rp 18.6 Trillion Share Buybacks, BRI Danareksa Sekuritas Says
body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas (BRIDS) notes that at least 10 issuers are preparing share buyback programs totaling up to Rp 18.6 trillion, adding demand-side support amid market volatility. Five new programs worth Rp 4.5 trillion from DSSA, BREN, BRPT, TPIA, and CUAN began between October 19-23, shortly after the market correction on October 16, providing about Rp 1.8 trillion of support per month over 2-3 months. Companies affiliated with Prajogo lead with Rp 3.5 trillion, as BREN, BRPT, TPIA, and CUAN hold 78% of the new program funds, active until December 31, 2026. Large banks have committed Rp 10.1 trillion, or 54% of the total, with BBCA the largest at Rp 5.0 trillion, followed by BBRI at Rp 3.0 trillion, while annual programs from BBCA, TLKM, BMRI, and BBNI run at about Rp 0.9 trillion per month. BRIDS notes that buyback values are maximum limits and actual realization may be smaller.

title: IHSG Recovers to Close Nearly 1% Higher After Early Decline
body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed at 5,328.36 on Wednesday (21/10/2026), up 0.94% after a volatile session in which it fell more than 1% intraday and ended Session I down about 0.8%. A key positive catalyst was Bank Indonesia's October RDG decision to hold its benchmark rate at 5.75%, below the Bloomberg consensus median projection of 5.88%. Large-capitalization stocks led the gain, with PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk (BREN) contributing 6.25 points, PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM) 5.56 points, PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) 4.94 points, PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) 3.23 points, and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk 2.96 points. Top laggards included PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (EMAS) subtracting 3.72 points, PT Ekamas Mora Republik Tbk (MORA) 3.33 points, PT DCI Indonesia Tbk (DCII) 1.85 points, PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) 1.49 points, and PT Energi Mega Persada Tbk 1.29 points, while Asian bourses were mixed.

title: Bank Stocks Rally as Bank Indonesia Holds BI Rate at 5.75%
body: Banking stocks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange rose after Bank Indonesia's October Board of Governors Meeting decided to keep the benchmark rate at 5.75%, below the Bloomberg consensus median of 5.88%. PT Bank Tabungan Negara (Persero) Tbk (BBTN) jumped 3.89% to Rp 935 and PT Bank Permata Tbk (BNLI) surged 3.83%, while PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) climbed 1.79% to Rp 2,840. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) added 0.96% to Rp 5,250 and PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) gained 0.27% to Rp 3,700. Mirae Asset Sekuritas Indonesia noted that holding the rate with convincing communication on rupiah stability could support banking stocks and the bond market.

title: 10 Issuers Prepare Rp 18.6 Trillion Share Buybacks After IHSG Plunge
body: Ten Indonesian issuers are preparing share buyback programs totaling Rp 18.6 trillion, which BRI Danareksa Sekuritas says should support buying interest amid rising volatility. Five new buybacks worth Rp 4.5 trillion, starting October 19-23, 2026, shortly after the market's sharp correction on October 16, 2026, come from PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA), PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk (BREN), PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT), PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA), and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN), running through December 31, 2026. Four of these issuers affiliated with businessman Prajogo Pangestu—BREN, BRPT, TPIA, and CUAN—account for about 78 percent of the new funds with a combined Rp 3.5 trillion. Big banks remain the largest overall contributors, committing Rp 10.1 trillion or 54 percent of the total, led by PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) with Rp 5 trillion, followed by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) with Rp 3 trillion. BRI Danareksa noted the announced buyback values represent maximum limits that may be used.

title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) Rebounds 9.84% After Sharp Declines, Trading Below 10-Year Valuation Averages
body: Shares of PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) jumped 9.84% to Rp 2,790 in trading on Tuesday (20/10/2026), after falling 14.84% on 16 October and another 3.79% on 19 October, with 692.97 million shares traded across 116,809 transactions worth Rp 1.87 trillion and a total net buy of Rp 284.1 billion. Despite the rebound, BBRI's valuation remains unusually cheap relative to its 10-year history, with a price to book value (PBV) of 1.31 times, below its -2 PBV standard deviation of 1.53 times, and a price earning ratio (PER) of 6.9 times (TTM), below its -1 PE standard deviation of 9.66 times. The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) plan to exclude stocks with high shareholding concentration (HSC) from the composite stock price index (IHSG) calculation is expected to make large-capitalization bank stocks, including PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI), BBRI, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI), more dominant in IHSG movements, as HSC stocks currently hold about 18% of the index weight. After the sharp corrections, the three state-owned bank stocks offer relatively high dividend yields, with BMRI at around 16.1%, BBRI at 13.6%, and BBNI at 11.8%, and all three have paid dividends for 18 consecutive years.

title: Foreign Investors Net Sell Rp 2.19 Trillion as IHSG Jumps 5.65%, with TLKM Quietly Accumulated
body: Foreign investors posted a jumbo net sell of Rp 2.19 trillion across all markets on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) on Tuesday (20/10/2026), even as the IHSG surged 282.2 points (5.65%) to close at 5,278.8. The largest foreign net sells hit PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) at Rp 966.1 billion, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) at Rp 355.39 billion, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) at Rp 269.8 billion, PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) at Rp 125.6 billion, PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) at Rp 117.8 billion, and PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk (ICBP) at Rp 107.3 billion. In contrast, the biggest foreign net buys went to PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) at Rp 254.9 billion and PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) at Rp 98.49 billion. Pilarmas Investindo Sekuritas attributed the rebound to regulator efforts to restore investor confidence after MSCI warned Indonesia's status could be downgraded from emerging market to standalone market, with the IDX designing a new IHSG calculation mechanism excluding issuers with high shareholding concentration (HSC) following a meeting between the IDX and MSCI. Year-to-date foreign net sell has risen to Rp 92.1 trillion, while total market transaction value reached Rp 26.3 trillion.
